subject: HarborCare: compliance licensing & pricing split — audit log retainer vs usage surcharge
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@harborcare.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: HarborCare Procurement <procurement@harborcare.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify compliance add-on pricing: audit logs, HSM seats, residency, HIPAA

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Procurement asked us to get a clean breakdown for the compliance/security add-ons before we proceed to SOW. Can you confirm the following in writing so we can map to our internal cost model?

1) Audit logs: current SKU shows 12-month retention included. Our security team needs 3 years. What are the pricing options — is there a flat retainer for extended retention, or is it billed per GB/month? Any discounts for committed retention?

2) KMS/HSM: do you price this as an HSM "seat" (monthly) or per-key/operation? We've had other vendors charge a flat seat + per-request fees. We need example math for 100k key operations/month.

3) Data residency: we want EU residency for a subset of traffic. Is that a one-time migration/setup fee, an ongoing residency surcharge, or a region-commit model? If there is a commit, what discounting tiers do you offer?

4) HIPAA: we need continuous attestation and quarterly evidence delivery. Is the HIPAA/assurance add-on a one-time attestation fee or recurring? What cadence for evidence delivery and is that included in the price?

Attached is our compliance requirements spreadsheet — can you propose 2–3 packaging options (pilot, standard, enterprise) and the associated discounts if we commit 12 months? Procurement would like a clear path to a concession if necessary.

Samira
Senior Security Program Manager
HarborCare

Attachments: hc_compliance_req.pdf (pdf, 230KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@harborcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify compliance add-on pricing: audit logs, HSM seats, residency, HIPAA

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Laura (legal/ops) to validate. High level, here are three distinct packaging options and an initial counter to help procurement model the economics. I attached a quick spreadsheet with the numbers.

Option A — Pilot (6 months)
- Audit logs: 6-month extended retention included up to 1 TB/month. Additional GBs charged at $0.08/GB/month.
- HSM: single HSM seat at $9,000/mo, no per-op charge up to 150k ops/mo; overage $0.02/op.
- Residency: EU pilot (90 days) included for up to 2 regions; afterwards standard per-region surcharge $2,500/mo.
- HIPAA evidence: one-time onboarding attestation $6,000; quarterly evidence pack included.

Option B — Standard (12-month commit) — recommended for cost predictability
- Audit logs: 3-year retention via an "auditlog-retainer" at $6,500/mo (covers up to 2 TB/month), overage $0.05/GB.
- HSM: seat pricing at $8,000/mo; if you commit 12 months and >= $150k ARR, we can offer a 15% discount on seat price. Per-op fees apply above thresholds at $0.015/op.
- Residency: 12-month region commit option: waive setup fee, shrink surcharge to $1,250/mo per region if you commit capacity for the region.
- HIPAA: recurring assurance add-on at $1,200/mo for ongoing quarterly evidence and SOC/HIPAA artifacts; onboarding attestation waived for 12-month commit.

Option C — Enterprise (annual multi-region commitment)
- Audit logs: enterprise retainer with flexible retention and volume tiering; price on request (typical effective $0.03–0.04/GB with large commits).
- HSM: enterprise negotiated seat + volume discounts; possibility of hybrid pricing (lower seat + lower per-op).
- Residency: included in enterprise multi-region contract with SLA and data isolation.
- HIPAA: full compliance pack + dedicated compliance SLAs and annual attestation cadence.

Counter/concession framework for procurement:
- We can provide up to 15% concession on HSM seats for a signed 12-month commit at the Standard tier (Option B) if HarborCare commits to a minimum annualized spend of $180k on Redwood services (total usage + addons).
- For audit logs, we can pilot 3-year retention at Option B rates for first 6 months at 50% of the retainer so you can validate volume.
- EU residency pilot stands as above (90 days free), with an option to convert to the 12-month regional commit discounted price if converted within pilot window.

Next steps: can you confirm which option Procurement prefers and share a target concession threshold (e.g., % off HSM, or a dollar cap on audit log fees)? Ben and Laura, can you eyeball the numbers and confirm legal constraints on the onboarding attestation waiver?

Thanks —
Irene
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference

Attachments: compliance-pricing-options-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

From: Samira Khan <samira@harborcare.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Li <ethan.li@harborcare.com>, HarborCare Procurement <procurement@harborcare.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify compliance add-on pricing: audit logs, HSM seats, residency, HIPAA

Irene — this is helpful, appreciate the clarity. A few follow-ups from procurement/security after reviewing Option B: 

- Audit logs: procurement prefers predictable OPEX. They asked whether the auditlog-retainer can be split across a 12-month prepaid schedule with a small volume true-up at year-end (rather than per-month overage). Is that doable?

- HSM seat: HarborCare is asking for a 20% concession on the $8,000/mo seat price if we sign 12 months. Their counter is based on a procurement-comparable offer from another vendor; they also want per-op overage capped at $0.025/op.

- HIPAA evidence: security is OK with the $1,200/mo recurring add-on but wants a formal schedule for evidence delivery (quarterly + ad-hoc on request with SLA for turnaround).

If you can send a redlineable term sheet with the Option B numbers plus the two concessions above (prepaid retainer option for audit logs and 20% HSM seat discount or a middle-ground concession), procurement can escalate to legal for fast-track approval.

Samira

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 11:34 AM Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet...

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: HarborCare: compliance licensing & pricing split — audit log retainer vs usage surcharge

Folks — forwarding HarborCare's reply and their ask for a 20% HSM seat concession plus a prepaid 12-mo auditlog retainer option. My suggested internal position to hold while we prepare a redlineable term sheet: 

1) HSM seat concession: offer 15% (not 20%) if HarborCare commits to 12 months AND meets a minimum annualized spend of $180k (same as discussed). Rationale: seat economics are material and HSM capacity is constrained; 15% is our standard top-line concession for security add-ons.

2) Auditlog prepaid: agree to a 12-month prepaid retainer option with a single true-up at year-end. Keep overage pricing at $0.05/GB but apply a 6-month pilot 50% retainer waiver for the first 6 months (to accelerate proof-of-value). This gives procurement predictability while protecting us from unexpected volume.

3) Per-op overage cap: Accept cap at $0.025/op (higher than our $0.015 target) but only if they also commit to the $180k ARR threshold. Otherwise keep $0.015/op.

4) HIPAA evidence SLA: commit to quarterly evidence by default; ad-hoc evidence requests will be delivered within 10 business days and may incur a small effort fee if outside the standard pack. Laura — confirm legal ok with 10-business-day SLA and the fee language.

5) EU residency: keep the 90-day free pilot but add a conversion clause: if they convert to a regional commit within the pilot, we'll apply the reduced surcharge of $1,250/mo retroactively to the pilot period. 

If everyone agrees, I'll draft a term sheet for HarborCare with these positions and a clear concession ladder (15% HSM discount at threshold; 10% otherwise). Ben — can you run the numbers and confirm impact to margin (simple model) so I can include a recommended bottom-line?

Thanks —
Irene
